column1: # THE PRODUCTION COMPILER CONSUMES THE POLYC-SELECTED EMISSION ACTION.
# A SYMBOL DEFINITION IS NOT CONSUMPTION. This file records the
# CONSUMPTION evidence: the production object that performs the
# emission IMPORTS the emission accessor, the linked binary CALLS it
# from inside the emission function, and the emission function does NOT
# Every artifact named here was produced by the REAL production build
# of the authoritative checkout at the C2 working tree.
# SECTION 1 -- THE PRODUCTION OBJECT IMPORTS THE ACCESSOR
# The production object is compiled by the REAL production compiler with
# the REAL selector ON, from the REAL production source. The object is
# the one the production link consumes.

column2: UNDEFINED REFERENCE: the production object IMPORTS the accessor and the linker binds it to the PolyC subject

column1: # SECTION 2 -- THE LINKED BINARY CALLS THE ACCESSOR FROM THE EMISSION FUNCTION
# The call site is FUNCTION-SCOPED: the disassembly window is bounded by
# the _emitFile label and the next symbol label. A call to the accessor
# elsewhere in the binary would NOT appear in this window.
# SECTION 3 -- THE C REQUEST FIELD IS NOT READ IN THE EMISSION FUNCTION
# The C request field args->emit_object lives at CliArgs+0x70. The
# emission function's disassembly window contains NO load at offset
# #0x70, so the C field cannot be the authority on this path.

column2: src/cli.h typedef struct CliArgs, field order computed from the declaration
FAIL CLOSED: loggerPanic("hcc: the driver selected an invalid emission action (%lld)\n", emission); return;

column1: # SECTION 4 -- THE FAIL-CLOSED DOMAIN CHECK IS PRESENT IN THE MACHINE CODE
# The compiler does not merely receive the action; it VALIDATES it
# before using it. The range check is visible in the disassembly.

column2: the action code must be in [1,4]; code 0 (absent/invalid) and any code >4 branch to the FAIL-CLOSED path
NONE: there is no path from an invalid action to the legacy C decision

column1: # SECTION 5 -- THE POLYC SUBJECT EXPORTS THE ACCESSOR
# The subject is produced by the REAL stage0 compiler from the REAL
# PolyC driver source. It is the object the production link consumes.
# SECTION 6 -- THE BUILD REFUSES TO LINK WITHOUT CONSUMPTION
# The consumption check is a build-graph EDGE, not a report. It is
# verified by an ADVERSE build in which the production source does NOT
# call the accessor. The build FAILS with a distinct reason token.

column2: REJECT_POLYC_ACTION_NOT_CONSUMED: "the production object ... does not IMPORT _WpDriverSelectedEmission ... Refusing to link."
REJECT_DUPLICATE_ACTION_SOURCE: "the production object ... DEFINES _WpDriverSelectedEmission itself ... Refusing to link."
REJECT_MISSING_PRODUCTION_OBJECT: "the production object ... does not exist. The consumption check cannot be skipped: a symbol definition is not consumption."
REJECT_MISSING_DRIVER_SUBJECT: "the PolyC driver subject ... does not exist ... Refusing to link."
